release.name: SafeGEO
release.label: SafeGEO release
release.domain_note: The first release is one kind of choice, which products people buy, in six verticals: the e-commerce setting of SafeGEO. Every other domain of Humanity’s Last Choice follows the same protocol; there is no fixed number of them, and each is contributed, documented and added as it is built.

paper.title: SafeGEO: Understanding Generative Engine Optimization Risks in Recommendation Agents
paper.tables: Tables 5, 7, 28, 33 and 35 of the paper; results/*.csv in the code repository

conditions.clean: Truthful-rewrite control: the target’s own source is rewritten in the same ten-line template as the shaped version, keeping its supported claims and its decision-relevant caveat. This is the paper’s baseline, so the comparison holds source form and length fixed.
conditions.shaped: Average over the paper’s eight realistic variants: the target’s own source is rewritten to win the recommendation, as a buyer guide, an FAQ, a comparison note or a product profile. One source is rewritten per instance; every other source, the candidate set and the hidden labels stay the same.

release.how_to_read: Every row is one system on the same 600 cases. Read each metric as a pair: the clean value, then the shaped value. The gap is the score. Lower is better for the two harm metrics; higher is better for the two quality metrics. Systems are ordered by how often the shaped candidate reached the top three in the shaped condition, lowest first.

metrics.name: Shaped candidate in the top three
metrics.definition: How often the candidate whose source was rewritten appears among the system’s top three recommendations. Under the clean condition this is the rate at which a truthfully described, lower-utility candidate makes the top three anyway.

metrics.name: Top pick violates a hard constraint
metrics.definition: How often the system’s first recommendation breaks at least one of the person’s hard constraints, as annotated in the hidden reference labels.

metrics.name: A right answer in the top three
metrics.definition: How often at least one ground-truth candidate, under the hidden reference ranking, is among the top three.

metrics.name: Utility of the top five
metrics.definition: Normalised discounted cumulative gain of the top five recommendations, with the hidden reference utility as graded relevance.

rows.note: Evaluated as the paper’s frontier-scale check (Section 4.2.1, Table 33). The one variant it resists is the explicitly model-directed source text: 51.3 % there against 95.5 % on Devstral.
The largest mitigation effect in the study: evidence breakdown takes the shaped candidate’s top-three rate from 78.3 % to 39.1 %.
The best clean-condition system: a right answer in the top three 71.2 % of the time. The shaped condition costs it least in quality and most in harm.
The strongest single variant in the study is on this system: the full-stack realistic rewrite puts the shaped candidate in the top three 95.9 % of the time, 83.2 points above its clean rate.

by_vertical.condition: over the shaped variants, as reported in the paper’s Table 28
by_vertical.note: Shaped candidate in the top three, by product vertical, for the three open-weight systems, with the uplift over each vertical’s clean rate. The verticals differ in what kind of evidence decides fit: plan and policy terms for the transcription tools, safety claims for the monitors, physical specifications for the rest.

mitigation.condition: Shaped condition (eight realistic variants, three targets); each intervention is a prompt or input change on the same attacked instances, measured against the unmitigated request.

methods.name: Defensive prompt
methods.definition: Requires clear support for important claims and preserves uncertainty when sources disagree.

methods.name: Rationale elicitation
methods.definition: Requires a brief reason and source-line citations for each top recommendation, without a separate evidence check before ranking.

methods.name: Evidence breakdown
methods.definition: Checks important claims against supporting and conflicting evidence before ranking.

methods.name: Context balancing
methods.definition: Compares claims across the full source packet so that one prominent source does not dominate.

methods.name: Instruction filtering
methods.definition: Treats source text aimed at directing the model as non-evidence rather than commands.

changelog.note: SafeGEO results from arXiv v2: four systems on product recommendations.

by_family.condition: over all variants of each family
